docs.title: Open AD Kit
docs.text:
The deployment layer for the Autoware ecosystem: packaging its software into reproducible deployments, built for the path from simulation to in-vehicle systems.

Autoware provides the autonomy stack; Open AD Kit makes it deployable. It splits the stack along the driving pipeline into focused container images, so a deployment runs only what its task needs, and keeps each deployment the same from one host to the next. A release ships the CLI, the pinned component images and a catalog of ready-to-run deployments. A kit holds your packages, config overrides and services on top of one of them.

It also integrates Autoware Safety Island, which runs on real-time operating systems and automotive hardware in a vehicle; Safety Island Simulation runs its POSIX build in a container. Open AD Kit is not an OTA service, a Kubernetes stack or a fork of upstream workloads, and it makes no ASIL or NCAP certification claim.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The terms these docs use, one per concept. Each links to the page that covers it.

docs.title: Images
docs.text: Term Meaning Component image A published container image holding one or more Autoware functions, for example planning. Latest alias An image tag such as planning-humble that follows the newest stable release. Release tags (-vX.Y.Z) and digests never move. Digest pin An image reference by content hash (@sha256:…) instead of a tag, so the same image bits are always used.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text: Term Meaning Release One version of Open AD Kit, such as v2.0.0: the CLI, the pinned component images and the catalog. Catalog The deployments a release ships. openadkit list prints it. Deployment A named, ready-to-run stack for one task, such as Planning Simulation: a deployment manifest, settings and Compose files. A catalog deployment is one of the release's; a kit deployment is one of a kit's. Deployment manifest deployment.json: what the CLI needs to run a deployment and its Compose files do not say: requirements, data downloads, roles and the verify step. Verify step The check openadkit run --verify runs once a deployment is ready: a command in one of its services, or that service's own exit. Launcher The openadkit command: it finds the release or kit to run and hands the command to its CLI. Release manifest openadkit.json of a release or a source checkout: its deployments and the images it pins. Settings KEY=value variables a deployment runs with, mostly Autoware launch arguments and host paths such as MAP_PATH: settings.env, then settings.gpu.env with --gpu, then the host settings. run and restart apply them. Host settings The settings of one host, in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env. They are loaded last and survive upgrades. One-shot service A service that does its work and exits, such as the scenario runner. Its Compose service has restart: "no"; it may finish but not fail. Role What one host does in a split-host deployment, such as autoware or scenario, with its own services, Compose project, ROS domain and Zenoh endpoint.

docs.title: Kits
docs.text: Term Meaning Kit Your packages, parameters and services on top of a pinned release. openadkit new makes one. Open AD Kit itself is not a kit. Kit manifest openadkit.json of a kit: the release it extends, its deployments (each named by its key) and the images it pins. extends The release a kit pins. base The catalog deployment a kit deployment builds on. Only a kit deployment has one. Extension point One of the five ways a kit changes its base: settings, config overrides, the overlay workspace, extra services and image replacement. Config override Parameter and file differences under config/autoware/, merged over a package's configuration on every start; not a copy of the full file. restart applies them. Overlay workspace Your ROS packages in overlay_ws/, built in the release's devel image and sourced on top of Autoware. Integrator The person or organization that builds a kit. Reference Design An Autoware Reference Design: a Deployment Profile and a Reference Software Stack that others can reproduce. A kit holds its software stack.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Term Meaning Evidence cell One runtime test of a deployment on one ROS distro and topology, such as planning-simulation-humble-linux-amd64. Evidence The evidence cells run against one build. A release needs a run in which every cell passed. CI exemption A reasoned manifest entry for a deployment without a hosted evidence cell. It is not a passing test. BOM A release's bill of materials: the pinned Autoware release, component images and external images.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: Term Meaning Mixed criticality Running safety-critical and non-critical workloads on separately qualified execution environments. Here, the Safety Island's real-time hardware beside the containerized stack; the containers on one host share its network and are not isolated by criticality.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text:
A deployment is a ready-to-run Autoware stack for one task. The deployments a release ships are its catalog. New users should start with Planning Simulation.

Deployment Purpose GPU Architectures CI evidence Planning Simulation Plan and follow a route on a sample map with the built-in simulator; --gpu plans with the Diffusion Planner Optional amd64, arm64 Yes, in CPU mode Scenario Simulation Run predefined traffic scenarios in Scenario Simulator No amd64, arm64 Yes Logging Simulation Replay recorded sensor data through sensing, perception and localization Optional amd64, arm64 Yes, in CPU mode CARLA Simulation Drive in closed loop with the CARLA simulator Required amd64 Exempt Safety Island Simulation Planning Simulation driven by the Autoware Safety Island controller No amd64 Yes

All run on Humble and Jazzy except CARLA Simulation, which is Humble-only, and the GPU modes are amd64-only. CI evidence says whether a release runs the deployment end to end before it ships; an exempt deployment ships without that check. Evidence runs on every architecture the deployment supports. See the Evidence Policy.

Scenario and CARLA Simulation can also run as split-host roles, with Autoware on one host and the simulator on another over Zenoh (experimental).

docs.title: Every Deployment
docs.text:
Complete the Quickstart setup first, with openadkit setup --gpu for a GPU mode.

openadkit list
openadkit run planning-simulation
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit stop
  • Add --ros-distro jazzy to validate, run or build to select Jazzy; Humble is the default. fetch takes no distro: the data is the same for both.
  • Add --gpu for the optional GPU mode of Planning Simulation (the Diffusion Planner) or Logging Simulation (CenterPoint). CARLA needs a GPU, so its GPU mode turns on by itself.
  • Put host settings in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env; see Settings.

CLI & Maintenance covers the other commands.

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. To use your own, set REMOTE_PASSWORD in the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

The visualizer listens on loopback only. For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

docs.title: Stop and Recover
docs.text: openadkit stop stops and removes the deployment. To replace missing or incomplete data, run openadkit fetch <deployment> --force. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Your Own Kit
docs.text: Start a kit with openadkit new (Create a Kit). It extends a deployment without copying it and keeps only your differences. The Kit Guide is the reference for every extension point.

docs.title: CARLA Simulation
docs.text: Run the full modular Autoware stack against CARLA 0.9.16 in closed loop.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• amd64 host with Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04
  • NVIDIA GPU with at least 8 GB of VRAM, 16 GB recommended, with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the OpenGL/Vulkan libraries that openadkit setup --gpu installs. The default sensors (LiDAR, IMU and GNSS) used about 4.5 GB in a measured run; cameras need more.
  • ROS 2 Humble images; this deployment does not support Jazzy

Complete the Quickstart setup with GPU support:

openadkit setup --gpu

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run carla-simulation

run downloads and verifies the Town01 map, then starts CARLA and the Autoware stack. CARLA renders offscreen by default. run returns once CARLA accepts connections and the services stay up; this deployment declares no readiness check of Autoware itself and is exempt from CI evidence.

To run Autoware and CARLA on separate hosts, see Split-host Simulation.

config/sensor_mapping.yaml enables LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS. Camera entries are available but commented out.

docs.title: Drive
docs.text: Open the visualizer. In RViz, set a goal with 2D Goal Pose and select Auto.

docs.title: Stop and Recover
docs.text: Run stop also after a failed start, to release the GPU. If autonomous mode is unavailable, inspect /system/command_mode/availability and /diagnostics_graph/status. See Stop and Recover for the rest.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Open AD Kit packages Autoware Universe into focused container images. Each image groups closely related Autoware functions, and deployments run them as separate containers that talk over ROS 2. External clients use the Autoware AD API; the images use Autoware's component interfaces between them.

All images build on a shared universe-common layer; see Build from Source for the build graph. The image reference lists tags and platforms.

The runtime images hold what Autoware runs. They leave out what only a compiler reads, such as headers and static libraries, and only the visualizer carries RViz and its plugins. A kit compiles its overlay workspace in the universe-common-devel image, which keeps both.

docs.title: Component Images
docs.text: Image Services Deployments sensing-perception sensing, perception Logging; CARLA runs the CUDA variant localization-mapping map, localization map in all; localization in Logging and CARLA planning planning Planning, Scenario, CARLA, Safety Island control control Planning, Scenario, CARLA, Safety Island vehicle-system vehicle, system, api, safety-island-bridge, safety-island All; the last two in Safety Island simulator simulator, simulated-perception, mrm-state-relay, carla-interface, carla-map-loader Planning, Scenario, Safety Island; mrm-state-relay in Scenario; carla-* in CARLA visualizer visualizer All

docs.title: Sensing & Perception
docs.text:
Sensor preprocessing and object recognition, as two services from one image.

  • sensing — launch: component_sensing.launch.xml
  • perception — launch: component_perception.launch.xml
  • CUDA variant — sensing-perception-cuda builds the same packages with CUDA and TensorRT, for detection models such as CenterPoint. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Logging Simulation (--gpu) and CARLA Simulation.

docs.title: Localization & Mapping
docs.text:
Serves the Lanelet2 and point cloud maps and estimates the vehicle's pose on them, as two services from one image.

  • map — launch: component_map.launch.xml
  • localization — launch: component_localization.launch.xml

Planning, Scenario and Safety Island Simulation run only map: the simulator stands in for localization. Logging and CARLA Simulation also run localization.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
Plans the route and the trajectory, and publishes /planning/trajectory. Launch: component_planning.launch.xml

  • CUDA variant — planning-cuda builds the same packages with CUDA and TensorRT, so planning_setting:=diffusion_planner runs Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Planning Simulation (--gpu).

docs.title: Control
docs.text: Follows /planning/trajectory and publishes the control command. Control reads only that trajectory, so it stays the same whichever planner produces it. Launch: component_control.launch.xml

docs.title: Vehicle & System
docs.text:
The vehicle interface, the system diagnostics and the AD API, as three services from one image. Autoware keeps the AD API with the system packages.

  • vehicle — launch: tier4_vehicle_launch/vehicle.launch.xml
  • system — launch: tier4_system_component.launch.xml
  • api {: #api } — the Autoware AD API, the external entry point of every deployment: clients initialize localization, set a route and change the operation mode through it. Launch: tier4_autoware_api_component.launch.xml

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
The built-in simulator: a simulated vehicle and simulated perception in place of real sensors and vehicle hardware.

  • simulator — launch: tier4_simulator_component.launch.xml
  • simulated-perception — dummy objects, tracking, prediction and the occupancy grid map. Launch: planning_simulator/perception_simulation.launch.xml

On amd64 the image also carries the CARLA bridge and the CARLA Python client that CARLA Simulation runs in its carla-interface service.

docs.title: Visualizer
docs.text:
RViz in the browser through noVNC: RViz with Autoware plugins, Openbox, TigerVNC, and a noVNC server over plain HTTP. The VNC backend stays loopback-only, and so does noVNC by default; reach it remotely through an SSH tunnel. To serve HTTPS, mount your own certificate into the visualizer from a kit (the release mounts none) and name its files in NOVNC_CERT and NOVNC_KEY; it stays the same across starts, so a browser exception for it holds.

Set these in the host settings file:

Variable Default Values Description RVIZ_CONFIG /tmp/openadkit/autoware_launch/share/autoware_launch/rviz/autoware.rviz Path RViz configuration inside the container: the deployment's (autoware.rviz, or scenario_simulator.rviz in Scenario Simulation), with config overrides applied REMOTE_DISPLAY true true, false RViz in the browser; false opens RViz on your own desktop instead, using the session's DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY REMOTE_PASSWORD openadkit String noVNC password, required when REMOTE_DISPLAY=true. The deployments set this default; the image itself has none WEBSOCKIFY_BIND 127.0.0.1 IP address noVNC bind address. 0.0.0.0 exposes noVNC on every interface of the host: put an authenticated reverse proxy in front of it RVIZ_GPU auto auto, on, off Automatic, forced, or disabled VirtualGL acceleration NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY unset Paths Certificate and key inside the container; set both to serve HTTPS only

To open it, see the Quickstart.

docs.title: CARLA Interface
docs.text:
The simulator image's autoware_carla_interface translates Autoware control commands to CARLA and CARLA sensor data to ROS 2 messages. Launch: autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml

CARLA publishes its Python client for x86_64 only, so only the amd64 simulator image has it (Humble and Jazzy); CARLA Simulation is Humble-only and needs an NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: Logging Simulation
docs.text: Replay a sample rosbag through sensing, perception and localization. An NVIDIA GPU with at least 4 GB of VRAM is recommended; CPU mode detects objects by clustering instead of CenterPoint.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run logging-simulation         # CPU: clustering-based detection
openadkit run logging-simulation --gpu   # GPU: CenterPoint on CUDA (amd64 only)

run downloads the sample map and rosbag, and with --gpu also the CenterPoint models (to ~/autoware_data/lidar_centerpoint). The rosbag starts playing once sensing subscribes to its LiDAR topic, at 0.4× speed (ROSBAG_RATE), and plays once: openadkit restart rosbag plays it again.

run returns once the stack is ready: the services stay up and the AD API can initialize localization. openadkit run logging-simulation --verify then follows the replay: it passes once localization is initialized and the pose and the tracked objects keep arriving. Every release runs that check in CPU mode; the GPU mode is checked by hand on a GPU host.

The sample rosbag is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. It has no camera images, so traffic-light recognition is unavailable and detection is less complete than with a full recording.

docs.title: Stop and Recover
docs.text: To replace missing sample data, run openadkit fetch logging-simulation --force; it also refreshes the CenterPoint models. See Stop and Recover for the rest.

docs.title: Planning Simulation
docs.text: Run the Autoware planning and control stack on a sample map with the built-in simulator, then set a route in RViz in your browser. No GPU is required; with an NVIDIA GPU, --gpu plans with Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run planning-simulation         # CPU: the rule-based planner
openadkit run planning-simulation --gpu   # GPU: the Diffusion Planner (amd64 only)

run downloads the sample map, pulls the images and starts the stack. The sample map is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. and is provided for demonstration only.

docs.title: GPU Mode
docs.text:
Experimental

The GPU mode may change in a minor release. See Compatibility.

With --gpu, the planning service runs the planning-cuda image with planning_setting:=diffusion_planner, and run also downloads the Diffusion Planner v5.0 model from Hugging Face to ~/autoware_data/ml_models/diffusion_planner/v5.0. The first start builds a TensorRT engine from the model there, so it takes longer than later starts. The planner used about 0.8 GB of GPU memory in a measured run, engine build included; RViz renders on the CPU.

Control and the rest of the stack are the same in both modes: control follows /planning/trajectory, whichever planner makes it. See Autoware Architecture 2.0 for the planner. CI evidence runs the CPU mode; the GPU mode is checked by hand on a GPU host.

Known limitation

Autoware 2.0.0's Diffusion Planner can stop the ego up to about 2 m before the goal, so the route does not become ARRIVED and run --gpu --verify fails on the sample route. This is the planner's own output, reproduced with upstream's image (autoware_universe#13603).

docs.title: Drive
docs.text: Open the visualizer. In RViz, set an initial pose and a goal pose, then press AUTO in the OperationMode section of the AutowareStatePanel to drive the route. See the Autoware planning simulation guide for details.

docs.title: Safety Island Simulation
docs.text: Planning Simulation driven by the Autoware Safety Island instead of Autoware's own trajectory follower. Autoware runs on DDS domain 1, the Safety Island on domain 2, and domain_bridge connects them. No GPU is required.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• amd64 host: the pinned Safety Island release ships a linux/amd64 binary.
  • No GPU mode: the deployment's diagnostics graph belongs to the rule-based planner. validate and run refuse arm64 and --gpu.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run safety-island-simulation

run downloads the sample map and the pinned Safety Island release, then starts Planning Simulation's services and two more:

Service What it runs safety-island The release's actuation binary (FreeRTOS on POSIX) safety-island-bridge domain_bridge between the two domains, with the release's bridge-config.yaml topic contract

Autoware's trajectory follower is switched off, so the control command comes from the Safety Island alone. run returns once the bridge's healthcheck confirms it: the command's only publisher is the bridge, and the follower is not running.

Two messages are expected:

  • run warns that a config override adds autoware-safety-island.yaml, which autoware_launch does not have. The file is new: Autoware's main diagnostics graph without the follower's diagnostics.
  • The safety-island container logs Waiting for ... data until localization is initialized.

docs.title: Drive
docs.text: Open the visualizer. In RViz, set an initial pose and a goal pose, then engage. The vehicle follows the Safety Island's control command.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
openadkit run safety-island-simulation --verify

--verify runs the same drive-to-goal check as Planning Simulation, as the deployment's evidence cells do on Humble and Jazzy.

docs.title: Scenario Simulation
docs.text: Run predefined traffic scenarios with TIER IV Scenario Simulator. The deployment runs a scenario automatically and writes the results to the host. No GPU is required.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run scenario-simulation
openadkit logs --follow

To run Autoware on one host and the scenario runner on another, see Split-host Simulation.

run downloads the Kashiwanoha map. Autoware takes about 90 seconds to initialize; the runner then executes the scenario and writes the results to ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results (run prints the path).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Set these in the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/scenario-simulation.env:

Variable Purpose Default SCENARIO Scenario path inside the container Bundled example SCENARIO_HOST_PATH Host scenario directory, mounted at /scenarios ./scenarios OUTPUT_HOST_PATH Host results directory ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT Seconds to wait for Autoware before running 600 GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR Simulated seconds per wall-clock second; below 1 on a host that cannot run Autoware in real time 1.0 GLOBAL_TIMEOUT Wall-clock seconds each scenario may take; scale it with the factor 180 MAP_PATH Host map directory ~/autoware_map/kashiwanoha_map

A relative SCENARIO_HOST_PATH resolves from deployments/scenario-simulation/. MAP_PATH must be absolute; use $HOME rather than ~.

To run your own scenario, keep it outside the release. Create a directory, put the YAML there, and point the deployment at it in the host settings file:

SCENARIO_HOST_PATH=$HOME/openadkit-scenarios
SCENARIO=/scenarios/my-scenario.yaml

The default ./scenarios lies inside the installed release: files placed there mark the deployment as modified and are lost on upgrade or uninstall.

Scenarios must match the map, and the planning sample map does not work here. To use your own map, point MAP_PATH at a directory that holds the same files as the bundled map, which the CLI checks before starting: lanelet2_map.osm, pointcloud_map.pcd, global_map_center.pcd.yaml, lanelet2_map_provider.osm.yaml and map.map_publisher.yaml.

This deployment changes one Autoware parameter with a config override: a file that holds only the changed value, merged into the upstream parameter file on every start (config/autoware/autoware_default_adapi_universe/config/default_adapi.param.yaml).

docs.title: Split-host Simulation
docs.text:
Experimental

Split-host roles may change in a minor release. See Compatibility.

Run the Autoware stack on one lab machine and the simulator on another, bridged over Zenoh. A deployment keeps its name and declares its roles in deployment.json; each machine starts one role with --role:

  • scenario-simulation: --role autoware on one host, --role scenario on the other.
  • carla-simulation: --role autoware on one host, --role carla on the other; both need an NVIDIA GPU.

Without --role, the deployment runs on one host as usual.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Each role runs its own services plus a Zenoh bridge that carries the deployment's allowlist, in its own ROS domain.

Each role is isolated: its own Compose project (openadkit-<deployment>_<role>), container names and ROS domain. The roles see each other only through the Zenoh bridge, so both can also run on one machine for testing, as long as each listens on its own port (see below).

DDS stays on loopback (CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=lo) in the role's containers and in the bridge; a role ignores another interface in the host settings file. Only the ROS traffic on the deployment's allowlist crosses Zenoh: simulation time, vehicle status and commands, transforms, AD API calls, the enabled sensors and what the visualizer shows. Map blobs and camera images are not routed.

Evidence scope

CI runs Scenario Simulation's two roles on one hosted runner; two-host runs and CARLA are checked by hand on a lab pair. See the Evidence Policy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
On both hosts:

  • Host setup as in the Quickstart.
  • The same Open AD Kit release and ROS distro.
  • Layer-2/3 connectivity between the hosts and 7447/tcp open only between them. An allowlist is not authentication; do not expose the port to a WAN.

Fetch data on the hosts that mount it:

openadkit fetch scenario-simulation   # both hosts (the runner bind-mounts MAP_PATH)
openadkit fetch carla-simulation      # Autoware host only

docs.title: Configure the Bridge Endpoints
docs.text:
Create or edit the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env, on each host. Use the host's LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0:

Host Variables Autoware (--role autoware) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447 Simulator (--role scenario or --role carla) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<sim-host-ip>:7447 and ZENOH_PEER=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447

The Autoware role only listens and starts first. validate and run on the connecting role fail fast when ZENOH_PEER is unset; stop, status and logs never need either variable.

To run both roles on one machine, pass the endpoints per command instead, with a separate port for each role:

ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 openadkit run scenario-simulation --role autoware
ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7448 ZENOH_PEER=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 \
  openadkit run scenario-simulation --role scenario

docs.title: Scenario Simulation
docs.text:
Start Autoware first, then the scenario host:

openadkit run scenario-simulation --role autoware   # Autoware host
openadkit run scenario-simulation --role scenario   # scenario host

The runner waits up to SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT for Autoware over Zenoh before it launches the scenario. Results are written on the scenario host under ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results. The visualizer runs there too, so RViz takes no CPU or GPU from Autoware on the Autoware host.

docs.title: CARLA
docs.text:
Both hosts need an NVIDIA GPU. Start Autoware first, then the CARLA host:

openadkit run carla-simulation --role autoware   # Autoware host
openadkit run carla-simulation --role carla      # CARLA host

CARLA RPC (127.0.0.1:2000) and map loading stay local to the CARLA host. The interface publishes simulation time, the enabled LiDAR, IMU and GNSS sensors, vehicle status and transforms; Autoware publishes control commands. Cameras are disabled in sensor_mapping.yaml; enabling them requires an allowlist and throughput update. The visualizer runs on the CARLA host, where the raw LiDAR already originates.

docs.title: Allowlist
docs.text:
Each deployment ships its Zenoh allowlist in deployments/<deployment>/config/zenoh.json5, mounted into the bridge of every role. Entries are full-name regular expressions, not globs. Both hosts use the same file, since either role can own an endpoint. Review the list before routing anything new.

  • The visualizer's topics are on both allowlists: planning and control output, objects, the vector map marker, /robot_description and the AD API (/api/.*) its panels use. Zenoh sends a topic across only when the other host subscribes to it, so without a visualizer these stay on the Autoware host.
  • CARLA's processed point clouds cross at 2 Hz (pub_max_frequencies); the point cloud map is not bridged.
  • /sensing/imu/imu_data of the simple sensor simulator is on the scenario allowlist because autonomous emergency braking and autonomous-mode availability on the Autoware host depend on it. Without it the vehicle stays in PLANNING and the scenario times out.

After an Autoware update, check the CARLA allowlist against the live graph of a two-host run; CI checks Scenario Simulation's.

docs.title: Latency and Timing
docs.text: Cross-host simulation is timing sensitive. With a large round-trip time the TF stream jitters and control nodes log transform or collision-detector warnings even when scenarios still pass. Keep both hosts on the same lab LAN; WAN and VPN links are best-effort and are not the supported setup.

docs.title: Lifecycle Notes
docs.text:
• status, logs, restart, shell, record and stop find the running role from its Compose project, so you normally omit --role. When several roles of one deployment run on the same machine, status and stop act on all of them; pass --role to choose one for the other commands.
  • Running a role that is already up updates it in place. Starting the single-host deployment while a role is running, or a role while the single-host deployment is running, is refused: stop it first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If RViz shows no Auto button and /api/operation_mode/change_to_autonomous answers "The target mode is not available", a bridged vehicle-status topic has stopped flowing:

  • Diagnosis on the Autoware host: a state monitor logs a bridge topic timeout (for example /vehicle/status/steering_status topic is timeout), and /system/command_mode/availability reports autonomous mode unavailable.
  • Cause: restarting a single bridge or interface container in a running split can leave Zenoh routes half-created (a route is removed and not recreated), so the topic no longer crosses.
  • Remedy: stop the deployment on both hosts and start the roles again (openadkit stop, then openadkit run <deployment> --role ...). A clean restart restores the routes.

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text: How to build the Open AD Kit images locally and how CI builds them. Most users do not need this: openadkit run pulls the published images (see Container Images).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (openadkit setup supports Ubuntu only; elsewhere, install Docker with Buildx and Compose yourself)
  • Git; step 3 installs the tools that import the Autoware sources
  • Disk space for several multi-gigabyte images: universe-common-devel alone takes about 10 GB

The component Dockerfiles build on upstream Autoware images from GHCR and compile their package sets from a local autoware/src tree (step 4 below).

docs.title: Build System
docs.text:
Images are built with Docker Bake from components/docker-bake.hcl, the same file CI uses.

flowchart LR
    CORE["autoware:core-devel (build)<br/>autoware:base (runtime)"] --> UC["universe-common"]
    CORE --> UCD["universe-common-devel<br/>(builds overlay workspaces)"]
    UC --> COMP["sensing-perception<br/>localization-mapping<br/>planning, control<br/>vehicle-system, api<br/>visualizer, simulator"]
    CUDA["autoware:base-cuda-{devel,runtime}"] --> GPU["sensing-perception-cuda<br/>planning-cuda"]
    UC -.-> GPU

universe-common compiles the shared part of Autoware Universe on the upstream core-devel image and copies the result onto the lean upstream base image, so build tools never reach the runtime layers. Every component builds from it. The CUDA variants, sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda, build on the upstream CUDA images and add the universe-common install tree.

The published images end with a per-build Ubuntu security refresh. Components compile on universe-common-build, the devel image without that refresh, which CI pushes only to its build cache. Its digest changes only with its inputs, so a build that changes no Autoware source or component Dockerfile reuses the cached compiles and only refreshes and reassembles the runtime images.

Group Targets universe-common universe-common-devel, universe-common component all component images, including the amd64-only sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda planning-simulation universe-common plus the images Planning Simulation needs (local builds) default universe-common + component

CI publishes every image to ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit.

docs.title: Build and Run Locally
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit.git
cd openadkit

# 2. Install host dependencies
./openadkit setup

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

# 3. Install the source import tools; pipx puts vcs in ~/.local/bin
sudo apt-get install -y pipx python3-yaml
pipx install vcs2l
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. Import the Autoware sources this branch pins
AUTOWARE_REF=$(cat .github/autoware.ref)
git init autoware
git -C autoware fetch --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.git "$AUTOWARE_REF"
git -C autoware checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
# An Autoware release, built on its official images
python3 .github/scripts/export_autoware_lock.py \
  autoware/repositories/autoware.repos autoware.lock
export UPSTREAM_TAG="$AUTOWARE_REF"
mkdir -p autoware/src
vcs import --shallow autoware/src < autoware.lock
# Backported Autoware fixes, when the branch carries any
python3 .github/scripts/autoware_patches.py apply autoware/src
mkdir -p autoware/src/middleware/external
touch autoware/src/middleware/external/.keep

# 5. Build the shared universe-common layer (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl common

# 6. Build the Planning Simulation images (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load planning-simulation

# 7. Run with the local images
./openadkit run planning-simulation
  • --load puts the images in the local Docker store; without it, Bake only fills the build cache.
  • Local builds are tagged <target>-<arch>-<ros-distro> (for example planning-amd64-humble), which is the tag ./openadkit looks up in a source checkout. The arch follows the build host; when cross-building, set tags with --set <target>.tags=.... To use other images, set the *_IMAGE variables in the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.
  • For Jazzy, build with ROS_DISTRO=jazzy and run with --ros-distro jazzy.
  • To build a kit's overlay workspace against these images, load the devel image too and name its local tag for openadkit build, here on amd64 and Humble:
    docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load universe-common-devel
export DEVEL_IMAGE=ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit:universe-common-devel-amd64-humble

Other useful targets:

docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl                                # everything
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl component                      # all components
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load sensing-perception      # one image

docs.title: Build Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default ROS_DISTRO humble or jazzy humble UPSTREAM_TAG Upstream Autoware release to build on, the tag in .github/autoware.ref (e.g. 2.0.0); required "" UPSTREAM_REPO Upstream Autoware image repository ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware ROS_SNAPSHOT_HUMBLE, ROS_SNAPSHOT_JAZZY ROS apt snapshot the UPSTREAM_TAG images were built from. The build fails when they do not match; see ROS snapshot. Snapshots for 2.0.0

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
build-all-images.yaml builds every target with the same Bake file. The build matrix comes from .github/image-inventory.json, the source of truth for which images are built and for which architectures.

Jobs run in dependency order: prepare, then build-common, then build-components. Most images build for Humble and Jazzy on amd64 and arm64. create-manifests then combines the per-arch images into multi-arch tags. CI disables the local tags (LOCAL_IMAGE="") and tags images through docker/metadata-action.

.github/autoware.ref pins the Autoware release a branch builds on its official images. CI builds main and release/* pushes, keeps registry caches per branch, and scans and runs the evidence cells after each build. A weekly scan of main's latest build opens a GitHub issue when it fails.

docs.title: Testing a Pull Request
docs.text:
A pull request that changes an image's inputs builds the affected images, amd64 only, for both distros. A pull request from this repository pushes them to the CI package openadkit-ci, completes the build there with its base branch's other images, copied by digest, and runs the amd64 evidence cells on that build before merge. A fork's pull request cannot push: its images stop at the build and scan, and run in the cells after merge.

A change that rebuilds no image, such as a deployment setting, the CLI or a check, runs the cells against its base branch's latest successful build. A dispatch of evidence.yaml with source_ref tests another branch or commit. The cells take the deployments, CLI and checks from the tested commit and the images from the build. A pull request's run is never release evidence.

Releases promote one of these builds; see the Release Process.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: For maintainers. A release promotes an existing CI build of its branch; nothing is rebuilt. The Evidence Policy says what a build must pass and What the Gate Checks how a release checks it, and Compatibility what a version number promises.

docs.title: Before You Release
docs.text:
• The branch: main, or a release/X.Y branch created from a release tag to fix an older line. Its .github/autoware.ref names the Autoware release (for example 2.0.0), and the ROS snapshots in components/docker-bake.hcl belong to that release.
  • vars.RUNNER_AMD64 and vars.RUNNER_ARM64 optionally move the build, scan and evidence jobs to larger runners (for example ubicloud-standard-8-ubuntu-2204 and ubicloud-standard-8-arm-ubuntu-2204). Unset, they run on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-22.04-arm. Pull request jobs run on them too, so point them only at ephemeral hosted runners, never at a persistent self-hosted machine.
  • GHCR packages accept pushes from CI: openadkit, openadkit-buildcache and openadkit-ci under ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/.
  • secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN (Contents and Workflows write) is set when promoting a build commit older than later workflow changes; otherwise GITHUB_TOKEN is used.
  • The release environment exists in the repository settings: the publish job runs in it, so the reviewers required there approve each release.
  • Immutable releases are on in the repository settings: a published release and its tag cannot change. The publish step fails when a release it published is not immutable.
  • A successful build of build-all-images exists on that branch; stable releases and pre-releases both come from it. The build summary shows its build_tag. The release ships the CLI and deployments of that build's commit. A push that changes only the CLI or deployments starts no build, so dispatch build-all-images on the branch to release it; the release run warns when the branch has such changes.
  • A passing scan of scan-images exists for that build_tag on the same branch; it runs after the build.
  • A successful evidence run on the same branch passed every cell for that same build; it runs after the build. See the Evidence Policy.
  • Highlights for a minor or major release are in .github/release-highlights/vX.Y.Z.md. The notes of that release and of its candidates open with them; the rest of the notes is generated.
  • The docs on main describe the release: a stable release publishes the site from main as it is then. For the first stable release, remove the "not published yet" notes first, from README.md and docs/includes/first-release-note.md with the two lines that include it.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Run release.yaml on the build's branch with the version and build_tag. A release/X.Y branch releases with its own workflows and scripts, so a later main cannot change how an older line is validated. Its jobs run in order:

flowchart LR
    V[validate] --> P[package-bundles] --> R[publish] --> O[deploy-docs]
  1. validate: runs the release gates in validate_release.sh (version format, the build run and its age, scan results, metadata and file integrity, image coverage, passing evidence, registry digests, Git tag). A build older than 90 days cannot be promoted. Nothing is tagged if a gate fails.
  2. package-bundles: writes the immutable release plan and the runtime bundle for both distros.
  3. publish: writes the notes and metadata from the validated plan, attests the bundle, installer and metadata, and creates the draft with its assets. It then creates the image release tags and, for stable releases, the latest aliases (see Tag Reference), and publishes the draft, which creates the Git tag. A published release cannot be changed: a bad one is followed by the next version.
  4. deploy-docs: publishes the docs site from main when the latest aliases moved. If it fails after a publish, re-run only the failed job or dispatch deploy-docs: re-running all jobs stops at the draft step, since the release is already published.

The release plan records the exact image digests, aliases and assets of the release for the jobs after it; it stays in the workflow run. The release itself publishes release-metadata.json.

docs.title: What the Gate Checks
docs.text:
Before creating a tag, release validation looks for an evidence-summary-<build_tag> artifact and accepts it only when:

  1. The run succeeded: it is a completed, successful run of .github/workflows/evidence.yaml on the branch that built the release, in this repository and not for a pull request.
  2. It tested this build: the summary names the promoted build tag, and it tested the build's own commit, not another commit against its images.
  3. Every cell passed: the summary result is PASSED. A cell passes only when every level it runs passes, and a missing expected cell fails the run.

A passing rerun may supersede a failed run; a failed run never counts. There is no release bypass input. The release also requires the latest full scan of the build to pass.

docs.title: Autoware and ROS Distro Decisions
docs.text:
Every release, stable or candidate, is a build of main (or of a release/X.Y branch that fixes an older line) on the Autoware release tag in .github/autoware.ref. The release records that Autoware version; the build's autoware-lock.repos, resolved SHA and upstream image digests record the input.

  • Autoware: pin the latest stable Autoware release at the release cut. If it has a blocking issue, keep the previous verified pin and explain the exception, date and follow-up in the release notes. A fix that is already upstream can be backported instead.
  • ROS distro: defaultRosDistro in the promoted openadkit.json selects the default, and the evidence cells of every declared distro must pass. The gate never switches from Humble to Jazzy or drops a failing distro by itself: to change the supported distros, update the manifests in a reviewed change and build and test that revision.

docs.title: Release Metadata
docs.text:
The release workflow seals the selected evidence summary (result, build, commit, run URL and cells) in its release plan before packaging. release-metadata.json publishes that same evidence, the BOM and the CI exemptions. The bundle, installer and metadata receive build provenance from the release workflow.

The verification table in the release notes shows the passing-cell count, readiness time, arrival time and peak memory of that build. A release never searches older runs or releases; its notes depend only on its release plan. Missing metrics are shown as -, never replaced with zeroes.

See Verify a Release to check a release yourself.

docs.title: The Docs Site
docs.text:
The site documents the latest stable release. A push to main does not publish it: a docs change reaches the site with the next stable release, and a pull request shows its own preview. To publish a fix in between, dispatch deploy-docs.yaml, which builds the site from main; do that only while main documents nothing the latest release lacks.

A fork can rehearse a release with the same workflow: it promotes its own build in its own registry namespace and publishes in the fork. Validation only requires the registry and the package name that openadkit.json names.

docs.title: Backporting an Autoware Fix
docs.text:
Autoware releases come months apart. A fix that blocks a release and is upstream, merged on Autoware's main or in an open pull request, can ride on the pinned release as a patch instead of waiting for the next Autoware release:

  1. In the upstream repository, git format-patch -1 <commit>, and add a line Upstream: <URL of the commit or pull request> to its message.
  2. Open a pull request into main (or the release/X.Y branch) that adds it as .github/autoware-patches/<repository>/<NNNN>-<subject>.patch, where <repository> is its path under autoware/src (a key of autoware-lock.repos, such as universe/autoware_universe). The review is the fix's own diff.
  3. Every build applies the patches in order right after vcs import; one that does not apply, or has no Upstream: line, fails the build. The release lists them under Backported Autoware fixes, its bundle carries them as autoware.backports, and openadkit version counts them. The Autoware version stays that of the tag.
  4. When the branch moves to an Autoware release that contains the fix, delete the patch.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: From zero to a running Autoware planning simulation in about 10 minutes. No GPU is required.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) or 24.04 (Noble) with sudo access
  • 8 CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM and 50 GB of storage or more; see Host Requirements
  • curl for the release installer; python3 and tar are preinstalled on supported Ubuntu releases
  • A web browser: the visualizer runs in it, so no display server is needed

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
v2.0.0 is not published yet

Until the first stable release there is no release bundle to install. A source checkout runs images you build yourself; see Build from Source.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/latest/download/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install

The installer verifies the release bundle, installs it to ~/.local/share/openadkit and puts openadkit in ~/.local/bin. If that directory is not on your PATH, it prints the command to add it. The bundle holds the CLI and the deployments; images and sample data are pulled on demand.

Pin a version, or check the files first

For a reproducible install, replace latest with a release version and pass the same version to install:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install --version vX.Y.Z

To check the files yourself before running them, see Verify a Release.

docs.title: 2. Set Up the Host
docs.text:
openadkit setup

Run setup as your normal user; it asks for sudo only for host changes:

  • missing base packages such as git and curl
  • Docker, when the host has none; it never replaces an existing engine
  • your user's membership of the docker group
  • the kernel's UDP buffer limits, which DDS needs for sensor data (/etc/sysctl.d/99-openadkit-dds.conf)

It then runs a test container to confirm that Docker works; --no-check skips that on a host that cannot pull it. Add --gpu for NVIDIA deployments: it also installs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the OpenGL/Vulkan libraries CARLA needs, and tests the GPU in a container. It does not install the NVIDIA driver: install one first, so that nvidia-smi works on the host.

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

docs.title: 3. Run Planning Simulation
docs.text:
openadkit run planning-simulation

run downloads and verifies the sample map, pulls missing images, starts the services, and returns once Autoware is ready.

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

docs.title: 4. Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. To use your own, set REMOTE_PASSWORD in the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

The visualizer listens on loopback only. For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

To open RViz on your own desktop instead of the browser, see Visualizer.

docs.title: 5. Drive
docs.text:
In RViz, follow the Autoware planning simulation instructions to:

  1. Set an initial pose for the ego vehicle
  2. Set a goal pose on the map; Autoware plans the route
  3. Press AUTO in the OperationMode section of the AutowareStatePanel; the vehicle drives the route

docs.title: When You Are Done
docs.text:
openadkit stop

stop removes the containers. The images and the sample map stay on the host, so the next run starts faster.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Deployments — scenario testing, rosbag replay, CARLA and Safety Island
  • CLI & Maintenance — runtime controls, settings, upgrades and cleanup
  • Create a Kit — your packages, parameters and services on top of a deployment
  • Components — the images behind what you just ran
  • Troubleshooting — when something does not start

docs.title: CLI & Maintenance
docs.text:
The commands you need after the first run. openadkit --help and openadkit <command> --help list every option.

Commands are shown as the release installer installs them. From a source checkout, call its launcher by path: ./openadkit in the checkout, or <checkout>/openadkit in a kit.

Command What it does list, run List the deployments, and start one and wait until it is ready status, logs, shell, record Inspect the running deployment and record its topics restart Apply changed settings, config overrides and overlay workspaces stop Stop and remove the running deployment validate, config Check a deployment, or print its Compose model, without starting it fetch, clean Download or delete a deployment's data new, build Create a kit and build its overlay workspace setup Install the host dependencies install, upgrade, uninstall Install, move between and remove releases version Show the installed release and its Autoware release

docs.title: Run a Deployment
docs.text:
openadkit list                                    # the deployments you can run
openadkit run planning-simulation
openadkit run planning-simulation --verify        # then run its verify step
openadkit run planning-simulation --no-visualizer

run downloads missing data, pulls missing images, starts the services and returns once the deployment is ready.

  • Ready means the services' healthchecks pass, for example once the AD API is up (READINESS_CHECKS in the deployment's settings.env). run then watches the services for 10 seconds and fails if one crashes, restarts, exits or turns unhealthy; a one-shot service may finish but not fail.
  • --verify then runs the deployment's verify step, the check CI runs on it: Planning Simulation drives the ego from its start to its goal, Scenario Simulation waits for the scenarios' result. run exits with the step's result; the deployment keeps running.
  • --no-visualizer starts everything except the visualizer, for a host nobody watches: its software-rendered RViz needs CPU that Autoware lacks on a small host. CI evidence runs this way.
  • One deployment runs at a time, including deployments from other kits, even one with the same name. run refuses while another is running, or while another has left stopped containers; remove either with openadkit stop. The roles of one split-host deployment can run together.

Every run writes results/run.json in the deployment's output directory: the version, distro and images it started, the digest of the resolved Compose model, content digests of the config overrides and overlay workspace it mounts, how long it took to be ready and, with --verify, the step's result.

docs.title: Runtime Controls
docs.text:
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit logs map planning        # only these services
openadkit restart                  # apply changed settings, config overrides and overlay workspaces
openadkit restart --all            # recreate the whole deployment
openadkit shell                    # a shell in the api service with ROS sourced
openadkit shell planning ros2 node list
openadkit record /tf /localization/kinematic_state
openadkit stop

These act on the deployment running on this host, from any directory, so they take no deployment name. With several roles of a split-host deployment on one host, see Lifecycle Notes.

status and stop also see a deployment whose containers have all stopped, after a failed start or a restart of Docker. Its containers stay, with their logs, until stop removes them.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Below its services, status shows Autoware's state from the AD API and the visualizer address:

localization initialized
routing      set
mode         stop (autonomous available)
mrm          normal

A line reads no data while nothing publishes that state yet, for example before localization starts.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
restart recreates services as run started them, with the current settings, config overrides and overlay workspace, and keeps to the same readiness checks.

  • With no service, it recreates every service that takes config overrides or an overlay workspace, and every service whose settings changed. A changed parameter file, a rebuilt workspace or a new settings.env value applies without restarting a simulator such as CARLA; restart names the services it left running.
  • A running service that shares the process namespace of a recreated one is recreated with it, since it cannot outlive that namespace: CARLA Simulation's carla-interface, a rosbag that is still playing or a scenario that is still running, which then start over.
  • restart <service>... recreates only those services.
  • restart --all recreates the whole deployment, one-shot services included.

docs.title: Shell
docs.text: shell sources ROS, Autoware and the overlay workspace like the services' entrypoint. Give it a service and a command to run one command instead of an interactive shell; shell then exits with the command's status.

docs.title: Record
docs.text: record writes a rosbag of the named topics (or --all) to ~/openadkit-output/<deployment>/recordings/ (--output to change) until Ctrl+C. It runs as a copy of the running api container, so it joins the deployment's ROS domain and knows the overlay's message types, and the bag stays on the host when the deployment stops.

docs.title: Validate Before Running
docs.text:
openadkit validate planning-simulation --data

Without --ros-distro, a deployment command uses the Open AD Kit's default distro, or the deployment's first one when it does not run on that.

validate checks the manifest and the Compose configuration without starting anything. --data also reports each data resource as ok, missing, incomplete or outdated and fails on any gap. It follows the same GPU selection as run: openadkit validate logging-simulation --gpu --data includes the CenterPoint models.

config prints a deployment's resolved Compose model as JSON, with validate's --ros-distro, --gpu, --role and --ws; AutoSD builds on it.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
A deployment reads its settings from environment files, in this order (later files win):

  1. deployments/<name>/settings.env: the deployment defaults
  2. deployments/<name>/settings.gpu.env: GPU settings, loaded with --gpu and for a deployment that requires a GPU
  3. ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env: your host settings file

Shell exports do not override variables defined in these files. Put host settings such as MAP_PATH or REMOTE_PASSWORD in your host settings file: it lives outside the release, so upgrades keep it. A source checkout can also override component images there; release images stay pinned. A kit adds its own files to this order; see the Kit Guide.

Most settings are arguments of Autoware's launch files, such as VEHICLE_MODEL; the rest are host paths and options of Open AD Kit's own services. To change a node parameter instead, use a config override.

Directory Default Override Host settings ~/.config/openadkit OPENADKIT_SETTINGS_DIR (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) Results and recordings ~/openadkit-output/<name>/{results,recordings} OPENADKIT_OUTPUT_DIR Installed releases ~/.local/share/openadkit OPENADKIT_INSTALL_DIR Run records, which restart reads ~/.local/state/openadkit OPENADKIT_STATE_DIR (or XDG_STATE_HOME)

docs.title: Downloaded Data
docs.text:
Maps, rosbags and models live under ~/autoware_map and ~/autoware_data.

openadkit validate planning-simulation --data   # report
openadkit fetch planning-simulation --force     # replace
openadkit clean planning-simulation             # delete, after asking
  • run and fetch download missing data and update outdated data. Data is outdated when the deployment now declares other content for it, for example a map with a new checksum. They update only data the CLI installed, and not while a running container uses it. fetch always includes the GPU data.
  • fetch --force replaces the data even when it is complete, and is the way to repair incomplete data.
  • clean lists what it deletes and asks first; --yes skips the question, as scripts need. Answering no deletes nothing and is not an error. It deletes all the data the deployment uses, including data that other deployments share, such as a kit deployment's base; the list names them. The next run or fetch downloads it again.

The CLI marks the data it installs with a .openadkit-resource.json file, and clean and --force only delete or replace marked data. Data that was already there, such as a map you copied yourself, is used when it is complete, but the CLI never deletes or replaces it; move or remove it yourself.

clean and fetch --force refuse while that deployment is running, or while any live container mounts the data (including another kit or deployment). If data usage cannot be checked, they refuse as well.

docs.title: Your Own Kit
docs.text: openadkit new my-kit [--base DEPLOYMENT] makes ./my-kit, a kit on top of a catalog deployment (Planning Simulation by default) that holds only your differences. openadkit build builds the kit's overlay workspace in the release's devel image. See Create a Kit.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
openadkit upgrade --check   # report whether a newer stable version exists
openadkit upgrade           # install it

The new release is verified and installed next to the old one, and the openadkit launcher is repointed. The previous version stays in the install directory, so you can roll back:

openadkit install --version vOLD

A version that is already installed becomes the active one as it is, without a download, so this works offline; --force downloads and replaces it. Images of a version you no longer use stay in Docker until you remove them with docker image rm; docker image ls ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit lists them. A source checkout updates with git pull instead.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Stop running deployments first; uninstall refuses while any is running, because it removes the launcher that openadkit stop needs.

openadkit stop
openadkit uninstall          # keep previously installed versions
openadkit uninstall --all    # remove kept versions too

uninstall is for release installs; remove a source checkout with Git. It keeps your host settings in ~/.config/openadkit, run records in ~/.local/state/openadkit, results and recordings in ~/openadkit-output, and downloaded data. The host changes openadkit setup made stay too: Docker and its apt source, your docker group membership and /etc/sysctl.d/99-openadkit-dds.conf.

docs.title: Names, Directories and Output
docs.text:
• A directory instead of a name: validate, config, fetch, run and clean also take a deployment's directory, such as openadkit run ./my-kit. An argument with a / or a leading . is a directory, and the kit around it is used wherever you run the command.
  • Version: openadkit version prints the installed release and the Autoware release it pins; in a source checkout, the commit.
  • Scripting: list, version and validate accept --json. validate --json prints one JSON document also when the deployment is invalid ("valid": false with the "error").
  • Docker commands: commands print what they do in plain terms; add --verbose (or set OPENADKIT_VERBOSE=1) to also see the docker commands they run, status queries aside.
  • Tab completion: Tab completes commands, options and deployment names, from the kit around the current directory or else the active release; bash-completion (installed on Ubuntu by default) loads it from ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions in a new shell. The installer leaves a completion file it did not install alone, and openadkit uninstall removes only its own link.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Commands are shown as the release installer installs them. From a source checkout, call its launcher by path: ./openadkit in the checkout, or <checkout>/openadkit in a kit.

docs.title: A Deployment Fails to Start
docs.text:
1. Check that Docker is running: docker info.
  2. Check the configuration and the data: openadkit validate <deployment> --data.
  3. See which services are up: openadkit status.
  4. Read the logs: openadkit logs --follow.

If run fails after the containers are created, they stay so you can read their logs, running or not; openadkit status lists them. Remove them with openadkit stop, which another deployment needs before it can start.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text: Your user must be in the docker group. Log out and back in after openadkit setup, or run newgrp docker. Do not run openadkit with sudo.

docs.title: Docker Compose is too old
docs.text: openadkit setup stops when Docker is installed but Docker Compose 5.0 or newer is missing. Install Docker's docker-compose-plugin (instructions) and rerun setup. Ubuntu's own docker-compose-v2 package is too old.

docs.title: Missing or incomplete maps, rosbags, or models
docs.text:
openadkit validate <deployment> --data
openadkit fetch <deployment> --force

validate --data reports each resource as ok, missing, incomplete or outdated; add --gpu to include the data of a GPU mode, such as Logging Simulation's CenterPoint models. fetch always includes it. --force only replaces data the CLI installed; remove data you placed yourself, then run openadkit fetch <deployment>. See Downloaded Data.

docs.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit not detected
docs.text:
• Install it with openadkit setup --gpu.
  • Check the GPU: nvidia-smi and nvidia-ctk --version.
  • Restart Docker: sudo systemctl restart docker.

docs.title: Perception is slow
docs.text: The default perception image runs on CPU. For CUDA perception, run Logging Simulation with --gpu on an amd64 host with an NVIDIA GPU. The CUDA image does not fall back to CPU.

docs.title: Blank visualizer
docs.text: Wait 10 to 30 seconds after run, then reload the page. If it stays blank, check openadkit logs --follow.

docs.title: noVNC says "failed to connect"
docs.text: Open the page over http://. The visualizer serves plain HTTP unless you give it a certificate (NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY); with one, open it over https://.

docs.title: Port 6080 already in use
docs.text: Port 6080 serves the visualizer. Stop the service that holds the port. The deployments use host networking, so a ports: mapping in compose.yaml has no effect.

docs.title: Point clouds arrive at a lower rate than they are published
docs.text:
Large messages need large UDP buffers between the containers. deployments/shared/cyclonedds.xml requests them, and openadkit setup raises the kernel limits that cap them (/etc/sysctl.d/99-openadkit-dds.conf). Check the limit and whether the kernel drops packets:

sysctl net.core.rmem_max      # 2147483647 after setup
nstat -az UdpRcvbufErrors     # a growing count means drops

docs.title: ROS 2 nodes on another machine cannot see the stack
docs.text:
DDS stays on loopback by default. To reach other hosts, set CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE to the exact LAN or VPN interface name in your host settings file (~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env):

CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=eth0

The other host's nodes also need the stack's ROS domain, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=1, and Cyclone DDS (RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp). This applies to single-host runs; a split-host role always keeps DDS on loopback and reaches the other host through its Zenoh bridge. ROS_DOMAIN_ID separates traffic but provides no authentication or encryption.
